learn.title: Naming a piece of code
learn.body: A function is a named block of code that you can run whenever you want. You have already used some: `printf` is a function someone else wrote, and `main` is a function you write. Now you will write your own.

learn.title: Define, then call
learn.body: `greet` is defined once and called twice. The include line is left out here to save space.

learn.title: Defining
learn.body: A definition has a return type, a name, parentheses and a body in braces. `void` as the return type means the function gives nothing back. `void` in the parentheses means it takes no input. The body holds the instructions to run.

learn.title: Calling
learn.body: To run a function, write its name with parentheses and a semicolon: `greet();`. The program jumps into the function, runs its body, then comes back to the next line after the call.

learn.title: Why bother
learn.body: A function stops you repeating yourself. Write the code once, call it anywhere, and fix a bug in a single place. It also gives a name to an idea, which makes the program easier to read.

learn.title: Order of events
steps: The program jumps into `greet`, which prints Hello!
It returns to `main` and runs the second `greet();`
It prints Hello! again, and then `main` ends

learn.body: The compiler reads top to bottom, so define a function above the place where you call it. Prototypes, in a later lesson, remove that rule.

questions.prompt: What does `void` mean as a function's return type?
questions.explanation: A `void` function does work but returns no value.

questions.prompt: How do you run a function named `greet` that takes nothing?
questions.explanation: Write its name, parentheses and a semicolon.

questions.prompt: `greet();` is called twice. How many times does Hello! print? Type the number.
questions.explanation: Each call runs the body once, so it prints twice.
The braces `{` and `}` mark the body.

questions.prompt: Which is a benefit of functions?
choices: Write code once and reuse it
questions.explanation: A function avoids repeating the same lines.

questions.prompt: Where does a C program always begin?
questions.explanation: `main` is the entry point, and it can call other functions.

questions.prompt: Put these in order for a program with a `greet` function.
questions.explanation: The definition is read first, then main runs and calls it.
